::: {#exr-miller-taylor-log-one-plus-x}
#### Maclaurin series of $\log(1 + x)$

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.26.

Find the first three terms of the Taylor series for

$$f(x) = \log(1 + x)$$

at $x_0 = 0$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-taylor-log-one-plus-x}
Differentiating repeatedly at $x_0 = 0$:

$$\ba
f(0) &= \log 1 \\
&= 0
\\
f'(x) &= (1 + x)^{-1} \implies f'(0) = 1
\\
f''(x) &= -(1 + x)^{-2} \implies f''(0) = -1
\\
f'''(x) &= 2(1 + x)^{-3} \implies f'''(0) = 2
\ea$$

The Taylor polynomial of degree 3 is:

$$P_3(x) = x - \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{x^3}{3}$$
:::
